Hi Phil, 

I tried to analyze using second order model. This is a code of mine::
spec7 = 'G = 1-33
         CONSTRAIN = (1,a1,a2),(2,a1,a2),(3,a1,a2),(4,a1,a2),(5,a1,a2),(6,a1,a2),(7,a1,a2), (8,a1,a2),(9,a1,a2),(10,a1,a2),(11,a1,a2), (12,a1,a3),(13,a1,a3),(14,a1,a3),(15,a1,a3),(16,a1,a3),(17,a1,a3),(18,a1,a3),(19,a1,a3),(20,a1,a3),(21,a1,a3),(22,a1,a3),(23,a1,a3),(24,a1,a3),(25,a1,a3),(26,a1,a3),(27,a1,a3),(28,a1,a3),(29,a1,a3),(30,a1,a4),(31,a1,a4),(32,a1,a4),(33,a1,a4),
         COV = S1*S1, S2*S2, S3*S3'
speks <- c(rep(1,11),rep(2,18), rep(3,4)) 
sec.order <- bfactor(db, speks, spec7, 'graded', SE = T)

However, it doesn't work as you can see here:

I don't know which one the mistake because I use the modified model of yours in this group conversation. Here is the code:
#simulate data
set.seed(1234)
a <- matrix(0, 12, 4)
a[,1] <- rlnorm(12, .2, .3)
ind <- 1
for(i in 1:3){
  a[ind:(ind+3),i+1] <- a[ind:(ind+3),1]
  ind <- ind+4
}
print(a)
d <- rnorm(12, 0, .5)
sigma <- diag(c(1, .5, 1, .5))
dataset <- simdata(a,d,2000,itemtype=rep('2PL', 12),sigma=sigma)

# estimate by applying constraints and freeing the latent variances
specific <- c(rep(1,4),rep(2,4), rep(3,4))
model1 <- "G = 1-12
          CONSTRAIN = (1, a1, a2), (2, a1, a2), (3, a1, a2), (4, a1, a2),
            (5, a1, a3), (6, a1, a3), (7, a1, a3), (8, a1, a3),
            (9, a1, a4), (10, a1, a4), (11, a1, a4), (12, a1, a4)
          COV = S1*S1, S2*S2, S3*S3"

simmod2 <- bfactor(dataset, specific, model1)
coef(simmod2, simplify=TRUE)

Would you like yo help me in spotting the mistake? Thank you in advance
